main_body: Flat dark-green ground patch, 64x48 (4x3 tiles), with a repeating pattern of small mossy tufts and a few red and amber dots. It is not a standing object.
top_band: none. Every column is one uniform run, rows 0-47, L about 49-51. This is flat ground with no top/front structure.
evidence: This is a terrain tile (ground fill), so the 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply. There is no standing volume, no receding side face and no elevation drawing, so nothing in it breaks the view contract.

style.evidence: The ground has no outlines. The dark pixels are tinted green-brown, and the measured neutral share is 0%. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, but only because of faint one-step noise on the base. The base is a near-uniform dark green (L about 49-51) with a thin ramp of about 3 greens plus a few accent dots. The whole patch has only 12 distinct colours, against 80 for the reference grass. Its median of 12 colours per tile is also well below the grass reference's 26, though above the paving reference's 7. The same tuft and flower stamp repeats identically every 16 px, so the tiling is obvious, and the grass reference has more varied clumps and a wider tonal range. The patch reads thinner and flatter than the grass reference, so it fails on shading depth and variety.
